audit.whatIsWrong: The content layer named two abilities Aurora does not have — 'Passage' and 'Vile Feast' — across whys[0], spikes[0], spikes[2], early, late, wants.you[0], wants.you[1] and wants.foe[0], and mis-cast Between Worlds as a level-3 burst tool.
audit.why: Her kit is Spirit Abjuration (P, spirits that heal her), Twofold Hex (Q, 9/8.5/8/7.5/7s, 900, curse plus a recast that drags the curse back and damages what it crosses), Across the Veil (W, 22/21/20/19/18s, 700, leap into invisibility), The Weirding (E, 15/14/13/12/11s, 825, slow plus a backward hop) and Between Worlds (R, 140/120/100s, 250, leap plus a crossable slow field).
audit.corrected: Every fabricated name replaced with the real ability, its real cooldown and its real range.

audit.whatIsWrong: The full layer read Levels 1 through 5 as 'Skill' while the content layer and the packet gave those rows to Aurora.
audit.why: Twofold Hex is 900 range against Anivia's 1075 but comes back every 9s at rank 1 and heals her through Spirit Abjuration, and Across the Veil lands at 3. Anivia has no way to convert before Glacial Storm. Content and packet are right.
audit.corrected: phases[0..3].side set to Aurora and early ratings dropped to 4/10; the level 6 and later rows already agreed on Anivia.

audit.whatIsWrong: spikes[2] and whys[4] pinned Anivia's first-item spike to Rylai's, against the full layer's own itemization, and no spike carried a cooldown.
audit.why: Anivia's spike is her mana item and storm uptime. Aurora's are Across the Veil at 3 (22s) and Between Worlds at 6 (140s at rank 1, and only 250 range).
audit.corrected: Spikes rebuilt on the real numbers; the 250-range ultimate is now stated as the reason level 6 favours Anivia rather than Aurora.

audit.whatIsWrong: The decisive interaction was never stated: Across the Veil is a dash and Crystallize creates terrain that blocks dashes, so the wall denies the one tool Aurora uses to enter and leave a fight. Nor was Spirit Abjuration's healing ever accounted for in the trading advice.
audit.why: Anivia W flag: 'creates terrain, blocks paths and dashes'. Aurora W flag: 'dash — mobility that grounding and walls can deny'. Aurora P text: exorcised spirits follow her and heal her; the kit carries a heal flag, and _missing raises the anti-heal rule for this exact pairing.
audit.corrected: Wall-versus-leap written into breakdown.carry, dosFull[1], spikes[3], late and report[5]; the healing written into tradeBad, breakdown.feeding, whys[1], wants.you[2] and the itemization line.

audit.whatIsWrong: Itemization never mentioned Grievous Wounds despite Aurora's passive healing being the reason chip poke fails here.
audit.why: Spirit Abjuration heals her off spirits exorcised by her own damage, so an extended trade she survives is a trade she refunds.
audit.corrected: report[8] now names Morellonomicon, and wants.you[2] makes it the player's mid-game requirement.
sources: enemy kit P text and heal flag

audit.whatIsWrong: The full layer called Aurora 'he'/'his' throughout, and the page used the awkward internal label 'Across the Veil (Hop)' as if it were the ability's name.
audit.why: Aurora is female. The ability is called Across the Veil; the '(Hop)' suffix is a data-file artefact, not a name a player will see in game.
audit.corrected: Pronouns fixed and the suffix dropped everywhere the string was rewritten.

notes: Second matchup in this slice whose content layer was written against invented abilities — 'Passage' and 'Vile Feast' do not exist in Aurora's kit. The data file's internal label 'Across the Veil (Hop)' was also being printed to the reader as if it were the ability name; the suffix is dropped wherever the string was rewritten. Between Worlds' crossable field is described only as something she can traverse, since whether Crystallize interacts with that traversal is not in the kit text. Whether Flash Frost's stun can catch her during the invisibility window of Across the Veil is likewise not answerable from the data and was not asserted.
